subject: Deployment mode follow-up: latency & throughput qualification for EdgeWare
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@edgeware.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: latency & throughput qualification for EdgeWare

Hi Samira — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from today's call (15:00 PT):

Summary of customer constraints
- Hard SLA: 95th percentile response <= 60ms for single-token streaming on user-facing search.
- Typical query size: median 18 tokens; spikes to ~120 tokens for longer context.
- Peak sustained QPS target: 300 qps during business hours; occasional bursts to 1.2k qps for 30–45 minutes.
- Data residency: must remain in their VPC for PII-cleansed logs; model outputs may be stored in their S3.

Preliminary Redwood recommendation
- Hosted API for initial proof-of-concept to remove infra friction; but given 60ms 95th and 300+ qps targets, Dedicated capacity likely needed for production to guarantee latency SLOs.
- Private VPC/on-prem is an option if procurement requires full network isolation, but adds ~6–8 week ops lead time.

Questions we need answered to finalize recommendation
1) For the 60ms target, is that measured end-to-end (including client-side network) or strictly service RTT?
2) What percentage of requests require streaming token-by-token vs single-shot batch responses?
3) Can you share a small sample of your QPS timeline (weekday vs weekend, hourly spikes)? we attached a template CSV to capture this.

Next steps
- Samira: confirm definition of 60ms SLA and upload QPS sample to the shared Drive by EOD Friday (2027-10-08).
- Ben/Marissa/Karthik: run a quick capacity and cost sketch for Hosted vs Dedicated using the provided QPS distribution once received; deliver by Mon 2027-10-11.
- If procurement wants isolation, we'll include Private VPC lead-time and an ops checklist.

Attachment: edgeware_qps_template.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0198

--
Redwood note: I've flagged this as a Priority-Deal for dedicated-sizing; tagging Marissa for cost sensitivity and Karthik for latency profiles.

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@edgeware.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@edgeware.io
Date: 2027-10-03T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: latency & throughput qualification for EdgeWare

Thanks Ben — good summary. A few clarifications below: 

- 60ms is our end-to-end target as defined by product (SDK call to rendered UI token time). We understand network adds variance; the service RTT budget we can allocate is 45ms at the 95th.
- ~85% of requests are streaming (chat/search use case), the rest are single-shot.
- I uploaded a preliminary QPS snapshot to the Drive link you sent (file: edgeware_qps_snapshot.csv). The weekday pattern shows two large spikes: 11:30–12:00 and 16:30–17:00 local time. We see ~900 qps sustained in those spikes for ~20–40 minutes.

Procurement note: they prefer to avoid on-prem unless absolutely required; they will accept dedicated pools if we can justify the SLA and cost. They asked for an official Ramp & Ops timeline for Dedicated.

Let me know if you need additional telemetry.

Best,
Samira
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeWare Solutions

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-04T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Deployment mode follow-up: latency & throughput qualification for EdgeWare

Forwarding Samira's QPS snapshot — I ran a quick back-of-envelope:

Observations
- If service RTT target = 45ms (95th) for streaming, Hosted shared pools will struggle at 900 qps bursts unless we dedicate GPU slicing and reserve capacity.
- Dedicated 2x A100-equivalent pool with aggressive batching and prefix caching should hold 300 steady qps comfortably and sustain 1k+ burst with autoscale headroom, but cost is materially higher.

Cost/ops sketch (high level)
- Hosted API: fastest to launch, lower upfront, but needs a fallback plan (burst throttling or degraded quality) to meet SLA. Good for phased rollout to 10k users.
- Dedicated: guarantees latency for SLOs with reserve; procurement likely needs 60-day lead + E2E testing window.
- Private VPC: meets residency but we estimate +30% ops time and procurement friction.

Items for Ben to present to Samira
1) Short doc that maps observed QPS profile to expected 95th latency for Hosted vs Dedicated (include assumptions on batching/window).
2) Dedicated ramp timeline (procurement -> provisioning -> smoke -> canary -> prod) with dates.
3) Cost delta snapshot for 3-month pilot vs 12-month committed Dedicated.

I'll draft the ramp timeline and a one-pager on batching strategies. Ben, can you own the customer-facing note and include the deterministic SLA implications? Karthik, can you validate the latency math and pick a recommended GPU configuration?

-Marissa
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_deploy_mode_cheatsheet.pdf (pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@edgeware.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procure@edgeware.io
Date: 2027-10-05T09:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: latency & throughput qualification for EdgeWare

Samira — thanks for the QPS file and clarity on the 45ms service RTT budget. Attached is a short customer-facing note that maps your QPS profile to realistic deployment paths and the expected 95th latency windows for each. High level: 

- Short path (recommended for POC, 2–4 weeks): Hosted API with a reserved burst plan and synthetic traffic shaping. Expect mid-90s ms 95th for streaming at peak — acceptable for experiments but not guaranteed in all regions.
- Production path (recommended): Dedicated reserved capacity (estimated 2x A100-equivalent with autoscale). We estimate 95th service RTT ~38–48ms depending on token length distribution and streaming tuning.
- Isolation path: Private VPC for procurement/regulatory boxes — adds 6–10 weeks and +ops overhead.

Attached: "EdgeWare_deploy_mode_map.pdf" (we will share detailed latency assumptions next).

Would it help if we scheduled a short 30-min session with Karthik to walk through the latency math and the Dedicated ramp milestones for procurement? Proposed times: Tue 10/12 10am PT or Wed 10/13 2pm PT.

Next actions (agreed)
- Samira: confirm which timeline you want us to model (POC vs Production Dedicated vs Private).
- Redwood: deliver the full latency & cost workbook by 2027-10-11.

Thanks — I'll hold the calendar tentatively for Tue 10/12 until I hear back.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
